en: The Secret Dharma of the Acala Messenger Dhāraṇī, in one fascicle.

Translated by Imperial Decree by the Śramaṇa Vajrabodhi, a Tripitaka Master of the Great Tang Dynasty who was posthumously granted the title of Kai-fu Yi-tong San-si and the posthumous name Da-hong-jiao.
Thus, for those who wish to receive and uphold this method for accomplishing all benefits— the mind of the immeasurable power, immovable, holy Vairocana messenger:
First, one should practice four kinds of diligent application.
Restraining body and mind oneself so that mindfulness does not scatter,
with a firm resolve, one will swiftly attain realization and fulfill one's aspirations.
What are the four kinds of practices for self-restraint?
First, fasting; second, ingesting qi;
third, eating vegetables; and fourth, moderation in food.
Having prepared what one can according to one's capacity and having bound oneself by means of one's own person,
one should recite the root dhāraṇī exclusively until it reaches one hundred thousand (*lakṣa*) or even up to three hundred thousand recitations.
Furthermore, for one day and one night, he shall not consume even water.
He shall perform a vast offering to adorn the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) and,
before the painted image, burn *kṛmuka* wood— each piece the size of a thumb and twelve finger-breadths long.
Dip both ends in ghee and burn one stick for every recitation of the mantra.
Once one thousand and eight sticks have been burned,
even minor worldly matters will have their wishes fulfilled.
Furthermore, once the count of recitations is complete,
enter a sea, river, or great stream until the water reaches the neck,
and stand facing east.
Once one has completed three lakṣas of recitations each day,
all the fields of merit (puṇyakṣetra) cherished in one's heart shall have their wishes fulfilled.
One should ensure that the water is free from makaras, nāgas, and malevolent beasts.
Fearing that the power of the mantra might not yet be perfected and could be damaged by external influences,
one must perform the rite of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
If one constantly applies effort in the recitation, [the protection will be maintained].
The Immovable Messenger manifests his form;
his power is able to bind all ghosts and spirits,
and he is also able to break and crush all trees.
It can also cause birds flying in the sky to fall down according to one's thought;
it can even dry up dragon pools.
In debate and when confronting non-Buddhists or evil persons, it is able to subdue them all.
Furthermore, first wait for the time when the moon is about to be eclipsed.
Have the mantra recited until the required number is complete.
For one day and one night prior to the eclipse, do not eat.
Take fresh cow dung that has not yet touched the ground and construct a square altar measuring two cubits.
There are two meanings for "that which has not yet touched the ground."
First, one should receive it with a vessel so that it does not reach the ground.
Second, even when it has fallen to the ground, if it has not yet been defiled by dust or soil,
one should simply take up the upper portion that has not touched the earth.
One shall plaster the altar; once the plastering is complete,
one shall scatter various beautiful flowers as an offering and place the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra* at the center.
Take a calf of the same color as its mother and prepare curd from its milk.
Immediately take one *liang* of clarified butter and place it in a vessel of refined copper.
Use a ladle made of *kharjūra* wood.
Churn the clarified butter.
Begin reciting from the first day of the lunar month until three signs appear.
Regarding what are called warmth, smoke, and flames:
one who attains the sign of warmth can,
by taking [this medicine], eliminate all diseases.
One who attains the sign of smoke may use it to smear their own body; by doing so,
they can remain concealed and prevent evil persons from seeing them.
One who obtains the mark of the flame-flame,
by ingesting it, attains supernatural powers; the body is able to fly,
which is what is called the supernormal power of the body (*ṛddhi-vidhi*).
Regarding "the milk of an old calf":
this refers to a calf that has been born for more than a year;
though the calf is as large as its mother, it still consumes milk.
The calf’s coat color must be identical to that of its mother;
only then will the cow's milk be fit for use as ghee.
Furthermore, once the practitioner has recited one lakṣa [of mantras],...
He immediately went to the summit of a deep mountain and,
abstaining from grain and food, recited another *lakṣa* [of mantras],
maintaining an uninterrupted continuity of mind without allowing for any other distractions.
The celestial treasures (deva-nyasa) appear spontaneously.
Generally, there are three types of treasures: those of the devas, those of the spirits (devatā), and those of humans.
That which was buried by a human being constitutes a "great treasure" (mahā-nyasa) of humans.
That which is guarded by spirits and deities is called a "spiritual treasury" (śeṣa-nidhi);
it is also called an "earth-treasury" (bhūmi-nidhi).
That which is guarded by the various devas is known as a "celestial hidden treasure" (deva-nidhi).
If even the celestial treasures can be seen,
how much more so the treasures hidden in the earth and those belonging to humans!
One should perform meritorious deeds and enjoy [the wealth] according to one's inclination.
Furthermore, according to the ritual for subduing Māra:
using a ladle to take up cow’s milk, recite the mantra once and burn it once;
continue in this manner until one thousand repetitions are complete.
It can eliminate great pestilence within the nation.
To protect those who uphold the Dharma,
one should dig the earth to form a hearth and kindle a fire until it blazes fiercely.
Regarding the ladle-shaped vessel:
it is carved from hard wood with a head shaped like a ladle,
capable of holding the contents of a chicken yolk or less.
Its handle is straight and about two chi long.
Take milk in a separate clean vessel and pour it from this ladle while reciting the mantra over it.
In the western lands, when an epidemic breaks out, sometimes an entire household falls ill, infecting one another until they all die.
This phenomenon currently occurs as well in the regions of Wu, Shu, and Lingnan.
This dharma can subdue them.
Furthermore, take flowers from a hundred kinds of grass, mix them with ghee, curd, and honey,
and for each incantation, burn one portion.
Whatever clothing one seeks, such as these colors and patterns,
shall all be obtained according to one's wishes.
If one seeks crimson garments, one should burn red flowers.
All other cases should be understood accordingly.
Although inconceivable supernatural powers fulfill the practitioner's wishes,
one may nonetheless seek them by measuring one's own capacity and according to specific circumstances.
Then there will be no future regrets.
If one recklessly seizes what is not one's due, the spirit will likewise treat such a person with contempt;
though they may obtain it, it will not be held in esteem.
If one burns one hundred thousand *lakṣas* of honey and *mīlava*,
reciting the mantra for each as it is burned, one will attain the foremost official rank in the kingdom,
provided that one can accomplish what is possible to do.
What one seeks will surely be accomplished. *Mīlava* is a foreign fruit.
Furthermore, by burning *piṅgalā* fish-flower, one gains the affection and joy of all people.
Burn pine wood, anointing it with the three substances, and recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times.
One will obtain immeasurable followers.
The pine wood should be seven inches long, as thick as a finger, and split open.
By burning barley and reciting this mantra, one attains the status of a Great Man (*mahāpuruṣa*), as well as wealth, nobility, and mastery.
Barley refers to *yava*, which is the same as *aśvayava* (horse-barley);
it is that which possesses a husk. 1. The Method for Painting Images: Subjugation through Image-Painting, Part One. If one wishes to perform the rite:
One should face the image;
when the mind has an object of focus, the spirit responds to that image.
On fine silk, one should paint the Immovable Messenger (Acalanātha).
She wears a red robe with a diagonal shawl;
her loincloth is also red.
On the left side, a single topknot hangs down as far as her ear.
The left eye gazes slightly askance;
the left hand grasps a noose, while the right hand holds a sword held upright,
the hilt of which is shaped like a lotus petal.
With a sword hilt adorned with precious inlays,
she sits upon a jeweled throne; her eyebrows are curved,
her eyes are glaring, and her body is reddish-yellow in color.
An expression of wrath,
causing all sentient beings to feel fear and trepidation.
Once this image has been painted, [proceed as follows].
At the bank of a river or the shore of the ocean,
in a pure aranya, or within a clean house,
the practitioner shall likewise purify their body and don red-colored robes.
Visualize yourself as being entirely red in color.
Without distraction, silently beg for alms.
Once you have completed five hundred thousand recitations, [the practice is finished].
Take five-inch pieces of *jiangdouji* (a type of legume pod), ten thousand stalks in total;
silently burn these three substances before this image,
reciting with a sincere heart as you offer them into the fire.
The Immovable Messenger immediately manifests his own form,
causing the practitioner to see him; having seen him, [the practitioner...]
One attains the mind of the Tathāgata’s samādhi and constantly dwells in the same place as all bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, before this image:
Recite this mantra three times each day.
After six months, by making offerings of flowers, incense, food, and drink according to one's means,
all various aspirations shall be fulfilled.
If soldiers or bandits should come,
the practitioner should hold a single banner and recite [the mantra] one thousand times, then plant it at the location from which they approach.
Those rebels and bandits will naturally retreat and flee;
terrified, they will disperse.
Whether they are those who harm the state or harm the Buddha-dharma, they shall be enemies and evil persons.
Mix salt with clay to fashion its image;
inscribe the person's name upon its heart.
The form should be one cubit in length.
Recite the mantra once over it,
cut off a piece, and burn it; continue until it is entirely consumed by fire.
If that person does not submit, they will surely die.
Furthermore, take mandāra leaves and burn them;
with each incantation, recite the name of the wicked person.
If one burns [the substance] for a full one thousand times,
the person before will certainly lose their mind.
By taking cow’s milk and burning it for one thousand times, they shall be restored to their original state.
If one burns salt while reciting the name [of the person],
chanting once for each burning until it is completed one thousand times,
anyone within a thousand li will come when summoned.
If one burns agalloch incense continuously throughout the three periods of the day without interruption,
one will attain the highest rank within the kingdom.
The aforementioned rites are all to be performed for accomplishment beneath this painted image.
2. The Method for Painting Images. Furthermore, regarding the second method for painting images: first, paint Śākyamuni Buddha in the center;
on the left side, paint the youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī in his characteristic form.
On the right side, paint the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
with a beautiful smile,
holding a vajra in his right hand.
Below, draw the Immovable Messenger (Acala),
adorned with precious necklaces.
Once one has completed five hundred thousand recitations before this painted image, [the rite is accomplished].
Perform various services:
take one hundred thousand stalks of lotus flowers and [prepare them] with the three substances of ghee, honey, and curd.
Sprinkle [the water] together with the incense upon a single flower.
Recite the mantra once and immediately burn it.
Continue burning flowers in this manner until they are all exhausted.
At that time, the goddess Padmaśrī immediately manifested her own form and asked the practitioner,
"What is your wish? Whatever you seek shall be fully satisfied."
Furthermore, take one *lakṣa* of *sumana* flowers;
recite the mantra once and burn one flower, continuing until they are all consumed.
Immediately, a yakṣiṇī will appear before you and be available for all manner of service.
If there is anyone who encounters terror and comes seeking help,
one should take ash from a charnel ground, recite the mantra over it seven times, and give it to them;
by having it protect their body, they will immediately attain peace and happiness.
Furthermore, take ox-gallstone and recite the mantra over it seven times before the image.
Mix it with clear water and apply a single drop upon the forehead;
this will cause all who see one to feel joy.
To subdue all vināyakas, as well as the venom of snakes, scorpions, and the like,
take clean earth to form a paste and recite the mantra over it seven times.
The painful sores will be healed immediately at the appropriate time. 3.
The Method for Depicting the Messenger Individually. Third: If one wishes to behold the Immovable Messenger (Acala-dūta), [one should proceed as follows].
Furthermore, for those who desire that all manner of thousands of human affairs may be accomplished according to their wishes,
they should paint the Immovable Messenger (Acala),
his body being reddish-yellow in color.
The upper garment is draped diagonally across the body and is blue in color;
the lower skirt is red.
On the left is one with a single topknot, the color of black clouds,
appearing as a youth,
holding a vajra in his right hand.
The left hand holds a noose;
from both sides of the mouth, small fangs slightly protrude;
the eyes are wrathful and red in color.
Seated upon a stone mountain amidst flames,
one shall achieve all accomplishments through various mudrās and recitations performed before this painted image.
By emitting light and concealing one's form, one binds all ghosts and spirits, achieving complete success.
Even if there is no painted image,
one may do so in a pure place or within a temple.
If one obtains a clean room where no one causes disturbance,
one will then be able to perform recitations.
All worldly spirits, ghosts, demons, illnesses, fevers, and the like [will be pacified].
If one recites this seven times or up to twenty-one times, there is no ailment that will not be cured immediately.
Before this painted image,
one should prepare a clean clay ground and burn agalloch incense.
Take a clear mirror and place it upon the heart;
while reciting the mantra,
have a small boy or girl look into the mirror.
When he questioned them about what they had seen, they all spoke of the matters for which they sought blessings;
they said that one must summon the dragon spirits,
yet they could only provide their names.
Having selected pure boys and girls,
one recites the mantra over them;
then those deities enter the hearts of these youths.
He then conversed with the practitioner about matters of the three periods of time,
answering everything that was asked.
If one wishes to attain the accomplishment of Kaṅkara:
On the first day of the month, begin the practice.
Rise early and purify yourself;
scatter flowers before the painted image.
Prepare a mandala by smearing the ground with sandalwood powder.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times at noon and again at dusk, reciting it one hundred and eight times for each occasion.
It is best if one can recite extensively without interruption;
at other times, if one is unable to recite the mantra,
one should simply sit within the ritual enclosure (maṇḍala).
One may also recite it with single-minded right mindfulness whenever the time arrives.
When the fifteenth day is reached,
one should immediately prepare various kinds of food and drink as an offering.
One cubit in front of the painted image,
one should dig a pit one span deep and burn *arka* wood.
If one does not have the wood for the arduous training,
one may instead take one *dō* and five *shō* of white mustard seeds;
begin this from dusk.
Recite the mantra over apricot kernels and mustard seeds as many times as permitted;
once a single recitation is completed, cast them into the fire to burn.
The mustard seeds should be mixed with clarified butter (sarpis) to keep them moist.
After performing this incantation for burning until after midnight,
Kaṅkara immediately manifested his form and said,
"What service do you require me to perform?"
The practitioner replied, "From this day forward, you must ask Karṇa about whatever matters arise;
do not follow me constantly, wandering here and there.
In this context, *karṇa* means "to inquire about matters."
*Kalpa* means "to dispatch.
If [the deity] does not appear, one should resolutely recite the mantra of Acala;
one must see him and must not give rise to doubt.
By dawn, there was not one who did not arrive.
Having appeared, they were all able to receive various commands and assignments,
even down to being used for washing hands.
If one wishes to ascend to heaven or enter the mountains, the willow branch shall cause all these things to be attained;
it shall also support the practitioner and lead them away.
If one wishes to see the celestial maidens of the heavens of the desire realm and so forth, [the same applies].
It is possible for them to meet in the future;
how much more so regarding taking people or objects from the human realm, even including various kinds of food and drink.
This deity manifests in the form of a small child.
There are two kinds:
the first is named Kaṅkara, who is respectful and cautious;
the second is named Caṭaka, who is difficult to converse with and of an evil disposition.
It is just as when a person of evil character is in a lowly position;
though they receive orders and are driven about, they are constantly full of faults.
Yet, when there is no business to attend to, they head toward the path.
Go now and return again.
Do not say, "There is nothing here; go in peace.
If you were to say, "There is nothing here; go in peace," [you would be mistaken].
"Even if he goes away for a long time, he will not return again.
First, you must remember that you must never meet him by chance.
There was once a monk in the Western Land who served [the Master] for many years."
Once having erred, he did not return;
weeping and wailing in regret, he never came again.
If you wish to cause the Naga King Kulika to appear:
On the wall, draw a sword,
encircled by the Naga King Kulika; the form of the dragon is like that of a snake.
Zhongjian wrote this letter "A" (阿).
Within his mind, he also visualized this sword and the letter clearly and distinctly, while his mental focus remained unmoving. The messenger—
Recite one hundred and eight times.
Do this three times a day for a full six months;
it is better to recite more frequently.
Once the moon has reached its fullness,
the Nāga King Kulika manifests his own form in human shape and constantly follows him,
remaining at his service to carry out whatever he is commanded to do.
The root mantra of Acala’s messenger is as follows:

*Namo samantavajrāṇām | vikṛtadaṃṣṭra mahābhairava | miṣṭānna-ṭiṭṭibha-carcarāhara | ātmarakṣa-dara | jaturmukha | śvānarāgaka-kapiludhi-vajra-heṣa hūṃ | vajravajrodbhara hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* Whoever maintains this mantra, [shall attain success].
For six months, one should recite and chant without interruption during the three periods of each day.
One should maintain pure food and drink daily;
whenever one wishes to eat, one should first set aside one portion and place it in a clean vessel.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times while waiting for the food to be consumed.
Once the meal is finished, place this vessel containing the food in a clean location.
After the month has passed, the Immovable Messenger (Acalanātha) will fulfill all various aspirations.
The three periods are morning, midday, and evening.
Recite one hundred and eight times during each period;
this is called the method for receiving and maintaining the root mantra.
Furthermore, there is a heart-mantra for summoning food.
This Acala-krodha-rāja is an emanation of Vairocana Buddha;
once held, one shall receive his protection throughout all successive lives.
If one seeks unsurpassed, world-transcending bodhi,
one should purify the brahma-conduct and apply oneself with single-minded diligence;
then one shall attain various inconceivable samādhis, inconceivable realms, inconceivable supernormal powers, inconceivable eloquence, and inconceivable efficacious power.
Such matters are known only by those who have realized them;
they cannot be fully described.
This is because worldly people have not yet severed their worldly habits.
Even if they have committed various grave offenses a thousand times,
the messengers will all permit them to repent and will not immediately cast them away.
The Method for Binding the Boundary and Protecting the Body: First,
perform the *śaṅkha-mudrā* by grasping the three fingers from the middle finger downward of the right hand with the three fingers from the middle finger downward of the left hand.
Each person, using the thumb of their respective hand,
should pinch the ring finger;
having thus grasped them together.
Extend the index finger of the right hand straight upward;
bend the index finger of the left hand and press it against the second joint of the right index finger.
Recite the root mantra seven times over the mouth and circle it three times clockwise above the crown of the head;
according to the distance intended, the boundary will be established.
There is no one capable of transgressing it.
Next, perform the *kavaca-mudrā* (armor seal):
join the two hands and bring together the two index fingers and the two ring fingers.
Inserting the hands within the palms, interlace the fingers and extend the two thumbs and the two middle fingers straight upward;
joining the two little fingers together so that they form the shape of a three-pronged vajra is called the *Kavaca-mudrā* (Armor Seal).
Having recited the root mantra seven times,
first place it on the forehead, then on the right shoulder, then on the left shoulder, then on the heart, and finally on the throat;
seal these five locations to protect the body.
Before sitting down to perform recitation, one should first perform this rite of protecting the body;
it is likewise appropriate to perform it when intending to go out.
Next, perform the sword mudrā.
With the left hand, press the tips of the ring finger and little finger with the thumb;
extend the index and middle fingers straight.
It serves as the scabbard for the sword.
Furthermore, with the thumb of the right hand,
press upon the nail of the ring finger and the little finger.
Extend the middle and index fingers straight to form a sword,
and place it within the left palm.
This is called the Sword Mudrā.
Place it upon the heart,
keeping the tips of the middle fingers straight and upright.
Recite the mantra for Acala-dūta that dispels all evil poisons seven times.
Having completed the recitation,
move it to the crown of the head and recite the following mantra:
Oṃ ajara-kanabudha-ṭṭhakā hūṃ hūṃ ke ke taṃ gṛhe mahā-rīviśa-svata-hrīṃ phaṭ. If there is anyone who has consumed poison and is on the verge of death:
Perform this mudrā and mantra seven times,
and it will suffice.
If you wish to establish a boundary, ward off ghosts and spirits, or disperse malevolent clouds and the like, [do so].
Then, place [the hand] upon the left knee in the manner of drawing a sword from its scabbard,
and pull it out with force.
Circumambulate three times clockwise above the crown of the head at whatever distance one desires;
then, holding the sword upright between the eyebrows for a short while,
all will dare not violate [the practitioner].
If one wishes to perform recitation,
first form this mudrā; then,
opening the hands, take up the rosary and recite according to the usual practice.
Next, perform the Seal of Fearless Purity:
with the upper joint of the right thumb,
press upon the tip of the index finger.
Extend the remaining three fingers straight and recite the mantra seven times.
For whatever offerings such as incense and flowers one wishes to purify,
use this mudrā for all of them.
Pointing with three fingers at clear water and sprinkling it will purify [the area].
If there are those who are fearful and come seeking protection,
one should bind this mudrā beneath one’s robes.
Recite the name of the person before you seven times.
Once the incantation is finished, that person will no longer be afraid.
This is called the Seal of Fearless Purity.
Next, recite the mantra for inviting Acala:
*Namaḥ samantavajrāṇām, aryavajra mahākrodha ākarṣaya ākarṣaya kṛtāñjalīṃ dṛṅkariṅkuru namaḥ svāhā*. Then, place the previously described sword-mudrā upon the crown of the head.
Bend the tips of the middle fingers of the left hand three times;
recite the mantra three times to summon them, and they will immediately arrive.
Next, perform the noose mudrā (*pāśamudrā*).
With the thumb of the right hand,
press the nail-bases of the three fingers below the middle finger,
and extend the index finger straight upward.
With the three fingers from the middle finger downward of the left hand,
grasp the index finger of the right hand;
then bend the index finger of the left hand.
Press [the thumb] upon the nail of the left hand’s thumb and recite the *śūla-mantra* seven times:
*Namaḥ samantavaiśvānarāṇām āpāśa-pañjara hūṃ phaṭ*. Having recited it seven times, [proceed].
It is used to subdue all ghosts and spirits,
causing them to pursue [the practitioner] for one thousand two thousand li,
including humans, devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings.
Using this seal and mantra,
next perform the Lion’s Ferocious Display Seal (siṃhavijṛmbhita-mudrā) as before: extend the two index fingers from the nail-seal (nakhamudrā),
opening them and holding them straight upright.
Standing with the body in the vajra posture,
brandish the mudrā either to the left or right;
with angry eyes and a wrathful mind, recite the *siṃha-mantra* while uttering the sound "HŪṂ."
*Namo samantabhadra-rājñām oṃ ajara-kana-candra-satye hūṃ phaṭ*. Recite this seven times;
it can subdue all evil māras and the like.
By means of this seal, the evil clouds and rains of Māra were dispersed immediately;
once they had dispersed, he released the seal.
If foul winds and rain do not cease,
take thorn needles and mix them with white mustard seeds;
burn them while reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Furthermore, if one recites the root mantra one hundred and eight times,
not only will the wind and rain disperse and cease,
but the nāgas and devas will also return to protect the practitioner.
Next, perform the mudrā for the heart-mantra of the root deity.
First, form the eye-mudrā:
with the ring finger and little finger of the right hand, grasp the tip of the thumb.
Extend the index and middle fingers straight;
from between the two eyebrows at the forehead,
let the index and middle fingers hang down.
Moving downward gradually toward the hairline, draw it upward;
this is called the Seal of the Immovable Messenger of the Divine Eye. Recite the heart-mantra over it while consecrating it with the mantra.
Oṃ cīrakuṣapa bhyo svāhā. With a mind of wrathful anger,
chant while making the sound of the syllable HŪṂ and calling out the name of the enemy.
The great spirit will seize that person’s heart and cause them to submit.
If one constantly recites this without interruption,
one will certainly attain the supernormal power of the eye and see the trichiliocosm.
And the affairs within the three realms appear as if before one's eyes, without any difference.
Next, perform the fundamental heart-seal (mūla-hṛdaya-mudrā).
Join the two hands in *añjali* and interlace them so that the tips of all ten fingers enter within the palms; then,
extend the two index fingers straight upward with their tips touching one another.
Grasp the two ring fingers with the two thumbs;
this is called the Root Mudrā. Recite the heart mantra as follows:

*Namo samantamukhānām trātāramogha-jñāna-mahā-rūṣaṇa-svabhāva-trāṭa hūṃ trāṭaya trāṭaya hūṃ trāṭa trāṭa ḍiṃ maḥ.* Every day, before eating one's own food, first set aside a portion of various kinds of food and drink.
Place it in a single bowl;
wait until the meal is finished, then recite the mantra seven times over it and pour it out into a clean place.
Every day, wherever one goes, one will always receive protection following behind.
Furthermore, there is a single-syllable mantra:
*Namaḥ samantabhadra-rājñām*. Use the previously mentioned root mudrā and mantra for this.
One should constantly recite and perform mudrās without interruption,
never departing from them for even a moment.
For the Mudrā of the Immovable Jewel Mountain, the ten fingers of both hands are interlaced with the tips pointing inward.
Quickly clenching the hands into fists is called the Seal of the Immovable Jewel Mountain (*acalagiri-mudrā*).
For the head seal, bend the right thumb and place it within the palm.
Forming a fist by grasping with the four fingers and placing it upon the crown of the head is called the Head Seal (mūrdha-mudrā).
The Single Topknot Seal (ekajaṭā-mudrā) is this very same Head Seal.
Extend the index and middle fingers upward,
place them side by side upon the left crown of the head,
and then draw them downward.
Below the ear is called the Sealer of the Single Topknot of the Messenger.
For the seal of the mouth, the two hands are placed side by side.
Interlace the two little fingers;
bend the two ring fingers and grasp the second joints of the little fingers.
With the two thumbs, pinch the nails of the two ring fingers;
the tips of the two middle fingers touch one another.
Bend the two index fingers and press against the third phalanges on the backs of the two middle fingers,
which are the third from the palm when counting upward.
Placing this mudrā upon the mouth is called the mouth-mudrā.
Next, perform the heart-mudrā,
following the same procedure as the mouth-mudrā.
Bend the two middle fingers and insert them into the roots of the two thumbs;
place them at the heart in the shape of a single-pronged vajra.
This is called the Heart Mudrā.
Next, perform the flame mudrā:
press the thumb of the right hand upon the nail of the little finger.
Form a fist with the left hand by grasping the thumb;
extend the index finger into the palm of the right hand,
and circle it over the head from the right side.
Moving to the left as if spinning, with all rays of light radiating outward,
this is called the Water-Flame Seal (Vāri-jvālā-mudrā).
For the Fire-Barring Seal, both hands form fists by grasping the thumbs.
Bend the two index fingers and insert them within the roots of the thumbs;
with the fists facing each other, keep them side by side.
It can eliminate all dangers from fire.
When reciting the previously mentioned Dharma Seal,
employ it according to the sequence.
Recite the mantra orally without ceasing;
maintain only the root mantra.
Once its efficacy has been established, for other mantras and mudrās, it is sufficient to merely recite them and perform the binding gestures, and they will immediately prove effective.
Furthermore, there is no need to maintain [this separately].

The mantra for universally encompassing compassionate rescue and immovability is as follows: *Namaḥ samantavajra-śāntana-mahā-rakṣaṇa-sphoṭaya hūṃ trāṭ ṭhaṃ*. This mantra is extracted from the *Vairocanasūtra*.
Having completed the preceding rites which encompass all mudrā methods,
one should then recite this mantra seven times.
Mentally recollecting Acala,
one also forms the aforementioned sword mudrā and places it upon the forehead.
At the left and right shoulders, the heart, and above the throat— these five places—
one should recite this mantra one hundred and eight times.
One should then visualize one's own body as having the form of Kumāra.
Then, snap your fingers and they will disperse.
Furthermore, there is a rite for taking the garments of a deceased person from a śmaśāna (cemetery) and painting the messenger Acala.
Having taken the blood from the body of the practitioner,
one should open and prepare it.
The painted image faces west, while the practitioner faces east.
Recite over this image;
bathe three times daily and, while wearing wet clothes, silently recite one *lakṣa*.
Once it is complete:
On the twenty-third day of the month,
the ritual for providing food and drink to all ghosts and spirits is performed.
Take various kinds of rice, various kinds of beans,
and sesame seeds; mix them all together to prepare a meal and scatter it in the eight directions.
Having fasted for one day and one night,
he seeks a corpse with all its physical characteristics intact and washes it until it is clean.
Having put on their clothes,
they lie down on their backs before the painted image with their feet toward the west.
Having burned incense to protect oneself and having completed the binding of the boundary in the four directions,
the practitioner sits upon the heart of a corpse and recites the mantra.
Once ten thousand recitations have been completed,
the dead person will immediately move;
there is no need to be afraid.
Simply press firmly and recite with urgency until a lotus flower emerges from the mouth of the deceased; once it appears,
take the flower and hold it.
He immediately transformed his body into the appearance of a youth of fifteen or sixteen years old and departed through the air,
reaching as far as the Brahma Heaven.
There is nowhere he does not reach;
he wanders with sovereign ease.
This is the method of distinct practice.
If there is a place of danger or fear,
or if one is oppressed by legal matters,
one should single-mindedly recite the root mantra.
One may also write this incantation on a nail and drive it into the ground within the courtyard;
ten thousand demons will dare not stir.
It is also excellent to nail this "Incantation of Compassionate Rescue" [to the door].
Simply purify the chamber, establish the boundary, and protect yourself;
fix the mind without wavering, O Messenger,
maintaining focused mindfulness without interruption.
It is even better to recite many times,
up to ten lakṣas. At every meal,
set aside one portion of food.
Make offerings to Acala and maintain the visualization within your mind with diligent persistence, never allowing it to be interrupted;
this is the most fundamental method for swiftly obtaining spiritual efficacy.
The benefits of this merit are as described; do not speak of them to others.
Furthermore, there are one lakṣa, or one hundred thousand recitations.
This concludes the essential summary of the method for the Immovable Messenger (Acala-dūta).
Below, it is recorded that he received it with faith and practiced accordingly.
The verse at the end of the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā-dhāraṇī* was also translated by the Upādhyāya at the same time.
If there are virtuous men or women, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, or others...
Whether one encounters misfortune or calamity, seeks official rank or noble title,
meets with a person of high status, or has someone requesting or seeking something,
one should cause the five fragrances to be burned.
Recite and maintain this until it reaches one hundred thousand repetitions without interruption.
If the days are short, you must make a vow.
Then many people shall share the same intention, enabling them to quickly attain the aforementioned number together and fulfill their vows. The incantation is as follows:

*Huiguang Pusa* (Bodhisattva Who Returns Light) *Huixi Pusa* (Bodhisattva Who Returns Joy) *Aneudaitian* (Anuttaradeva) *Zhide Pusa* (Bodhisattva of Resolute Virtue) *Youqiu Poqiu* (Yukṣu Pakṣu) *Qingjing Biqiu* (Pure Bhikṣu) I pray that for [Name], whether seeking matters for oneself—then state one’s own name—or seeking matters for another—then state the other person’s name—their official affairs shall be successfully concluded and their life-threatening matters shall immediately cease. May the various devas and bodhisattvas, and the arhats of foreign lands, rescue and deliver [Name] from calamities and cross over all hardships. Even if one seeks office, may it be attained.
"May it be granted that [Name] shall descend before me;
may they obtain such-and-such an office, their past karmic calamities forever extinguished and all obstacles and difficulties brought to rest."
Furthermore, following the passage "Also, for the sake of protecting such-and-such a person from calamities and delivering them from hardships," it says:
"May whatever is sought by such-and-such a person be fulfilled according to their wishes; may your compassion fulfill the disciple's aspirations."
The practitioner of the Dharma should first recite it until it is thoroughly mastered,
without making any sound with the mouth.
Once the count of one hundred thousand recitations is completed:
One will immediately obtain one's wishes.
If seeking swift efficacy, there should be no interruption in practice whether walking or standing.
For matters of great importance, many should recite together.
When going out, it is not necessary to burn incense;
however, when sitting at home in meditation, one must certainly burn the five fragrances:
benzoin, valerian, cinnamomum tamala, agarwood, and frankincense.
If agarwood is unavailable, it may be substituted with white sandalwood.
However, one must not omit agallochum or calamus.
